citations.review_text:
I'm a bit mixed on this game because I played the FES version on PS2 years ago. 

The Answer situation that everyone talks about is bad with this game, 100%. You can just emulate the FES version on PC and get the same content for free instead of having Atlus charge you $90 for it.

Atlus also screwed with the music where they got new singers or something and it just doesn't sound right anymore. I had a mod that fixed this and restored the FES music, but then the game updated and the mod broke so I had to delete the mod. Atlus, we already paid $90 for your dumb game, please give us a toggle in the game options that restores that functionality. We shouldn't have to pay for that.

Also I do want to preface this by saying that the reason I prefer this version over FES is because they either dumbed down or removed completely the "sick" function from FES. I can't remember. In FES, if your characters got sick they cannot go to Tartarus and while exploring that dungeon they got tired very easily. Tired characters got sick more frequently in FES.

The main reason I really love Persona 3 is because Tartarus is a full-on dungeon that you can explore to your heart's content. Having your character get tired or sick too quickly really ruins that experience for me because I'm here for the dungeon crawling. The simulation part of these games are second nature to me because that's not why I'm here. I'm a Megami Tensei fan over a Persona fan and that's why I feel this way. Removing that feature or restricting it makes this game a lot more fun than the FES version for people like me that enjoy dungeon crawling and grinding for that level up.

That's what really makes this the superior version of the game and why I would rather have the FES music on this version of the game.
just use an emulator. the game being $60 is fine, but having The Answer be an extra $35 is ridiculous

claims.claim: Reviewers describe Tartarus as repetitive and a grind, featuring looped floors, layouts, and enemies without meaningful storyline progression or world building between block themes.

citations.review_text: Persona 3 reload is a fantastic persona game and in a lot of ways can be considered the best. From an emotional and world building storyline this definitely outclasses the other titles. This is not your happy sunshine and rainbows persona game as it is dark, gritty, and will inflict a lot of emotional damage. It does a great job with its primary cast of characters and even handles the side characters well for a vast majority of them. The turns the story takes are also done incredibly well and keep you on your toes wondering what will happen next in a lot of scenarios. Gameplay is the only thing I have a gripe about. Keep in mind this is an incredibly streamlined persona game and easily the most respectful of your time when it comes to the gameplay itself. Exploring Tartarus is super stream lined and all of the animations are sped up to respect your time. Pick a card is faster, general menu navigation is faster, even chest interactions and combat animations are faster. The big problem with P3’s gameplay is that it plays like mementos in P5. It's the same looping floors, same looping layout, same song and dance but on repeat. It's a chore to put it simply and not a fun one at that. Unlike the superior dungeon layout like you find in P4 + P5 you don't get any world building, any impactful bosses, no meaningful storyline, it's just a bunch of pointless looped enemies and chests. It feels like a grind for the sake of grinding. It also doesn't help that you need to use a teleporter on select floors to go to the entrance just to save. Thankfully the overworld, characters, and storyline carry the game so much so that it's worth the slog of gameplay. Your teammates develop so much over the course of the game and they do a wonderful job developing each of them throughout the playthrough. Some of the side social links are done incredibly well and are some of my favorites across the entire franchise. I will mention that the soundtrack is kind of a mixed bag with this title if y…

Persona 3 Reload is a wonderful game bogged down by inexperienced developers.

I'll start off by saying, I love the Persona series, and I played Persona 3 Reload all the way through to the end, minus the post game DLC. I played Persona 5 Royal first and since finishing Persona 3 Reload, I've started playing Persona 4 Golden. Both Persona 5 and Persona 4 captivated me in ways that Persona 3 struggled to. 

Persona 3's strength is its story. I can see the makings of a wonderful game here. Persona 3's story is emotional, compelling, and for the most part, well narrated. That said, this game fundamentally struggles in other ways that make it, in my opinion, unsuitable for the average player. Persona 3's weakest point is in its gameplay. Unlike the later games which feature varied dungeons, Persona 3 has a single dungeon with hundreds of floors that you explore over the course of the game. The only problem is that you're teased with the mysteries and secrets that it holds, with little payoff throughout the entire game. Every forty floors or so the theme changes up a little bit, but otherwise it's largely the same, and it gets boring fast.

Another issue I have with the game is the story pacing. The story itself is great, but it lags terribly throughout most of the game and a lot happens in small periods of time. There's a central villain in the game who is literally only relevant for one in game day and then is barely spoken of again despite being responsible for much of the game's main conflict. 

The dull gameplay combined with the extreme lengths of time between story beats led me to take several long hiatuses from this game, and I didn't remember as much whenever I returned. That said, Persona 3 Reload still has a lot of good sides. The game is visually beautiful and the soundtrack is awesome. The characters are very likeable and have good chemistry—though not the best in the series. 

I definitely enjoyed Persona 3 Reload, but I don't think I could play it…

citations.review_text:
玩P3R之前玩过P4和P5R。

总体来说游玩体验还比较舒适，但通关一周也不会想玩二周那种。以下为个人一些碎碎念

感觉相对于后续两作，这一作的coop剧情个人有点糟糕，基本没有什么给人深刻印象的角色。有几个coop比如死肥宅，僧侣，田中社长感觉挺突兀的。仿佛有深度却没有深度。另外我感觉这一作的基友位顺平太没有魅力了，游戏到中后期基本从来不带他进队了（怀念你了龙司）。特殊关系女主我‘先’选了风花（对标p5r双叶，比起辣妹类个人还是更较喜欢这样的角色哈哈）。非女主角色里，我比较喜欢狗狗和正太。狗狗感觉战斗也挺强的。

总体人设上我感觉都还行。但不知道是不是我的错觉，感觉立绘好突出眼睑，让我感觉每个人都要把他们的泪腺（物理意味）怼在我的脸上。或许是我的错觉吧，但这点让我有一些不适。主角的设定我还是很喜欢的。虽然整体我感觉比起p5r还是差一些（毕竟是更早的游戏，也很正常吧）。

说起来，本作从头到尾只有一个大迷宫这点还是比较新鲜的。貌似挺多玩家不喜欢这点，我个人其实还可以接受。反正都是牢，统一在一个地方打的还是更快一些。

游戏流程上，刚开始选了最高难度，感觉打起来太累了，换低了一档，感觉就是我的舒适区了。基本全程也没啥卡关的。也没有像当初玩p4的时候那样查技能配技能，就随便打打，偶尔刷刷金手指拿点资源，通关挺顺利的。其实我还希望游戏能够特殊标注一下那些p是特殊p（需要道具或者coop解锁的），这样或许能让我有更大的合成最强p的动力。玩的时候感觉实在是懒得查资料，就摆了。

看到其他玩家有说这作剧情比较沉重。确实能感觉到，不过也就那样吧，以现在的标准看，我觉得都不算是特别黑的剧情。
Probably one of my favorite stories in a game ngl. Tartarus is a little repetitive but the payoff for getting through it was more than worth it for me.

[h1] A great remake from an amazing franchise [/h1]

Persona 6's reveal got me hyped to play this, and I ended having alot of fun. I don't usually play alot of turn based RPG's, Except Atlus' games. Main reasons for that are the story, characters, artstyle & music, and this game delivers all those in spades!

[h3] + Positives [/h3]

+ Story = The game mainly tackles themes of death & finding the will to move on. The dark hour phenomenon is a great plot thread that keeps surprising you till the end. Sad and bittersweet character moments, and the ending was near perfect! Almost got me choked up. 
+ Characters = I ended up liking almost all the characters. Very well written and voice acted (both English and Japanese).
+ Music = Persona always kicks a$$ when it comes to music, and this game is not an exception to that rule. Amazing, melancholic tracks with a spirinkle of hip-hop.
+ Artstyle = Jaw dropping UI design! They used unreal engine 4 to its full effect! lovely character models and usage of colors too! Good PC optimization as usual.. Ran smooth.
+ Combat = Combat is cool, albeit a bit easy at times, So I cranked it up to hard. All out attacks still feels satisfying to pull off.


[h3] - Negatives [/h3]

- Pacing = The main goal of the game is to climb a 260 floor building to reach the end boss, but I wish it had 60 less floors. It would've really helped with the pacing, as I felt the game dragged a bit in the end.
- Not many good bosses = There are "boss fights", but I felt the game lacked in cool boss mecahnics & fights. Most bosses functioned similar to each other.

[h3] .. Nitpicks [/h3]

1. Wish you could do more in the school man. The city also felt alot smaller than Persona 4 & 5. Not many activities to do. 
2.  Too many party members to select for a battle, but you can only go with a team of 4 (including yourself).

citations.review_text:
This was honestly a fantastic experience. I did not think I'd like this game as much as I did.

First, Persona 5 is one of my favorites games and I have played through it multiple times (including Vanilla and Royal). Persona 3 Reload is surprisingly much more stylish than I was expecting since the themes of the game is so different from P5. Honestly, the visuals of the game is a very pleasant surprise.

The OST is, obviously, stellar. The songs you will hear the most are very smooth and light, the battle themes are great and the music is very well used during the story.

The gameplay is awesome, the exploration is very linear and it can get a bit repetitive at times (especially if you tackle the Tartarus sections at once to save days for the social stuff), but I did enjoy the Gate Keepers and the much, much more limited SP management options. While the game isn't hard at all, it's still harder than P5R (which, again, isn't much).

There is a LOT of RNG in the game, though, which can get annoying. Farming late game materials can be grating if you want to make the best gear for everybody, and you do end up wasting a lot of time on resets and running around IF you want to chase (mostly unecessary) gear upgrades.

The Social-Links are mostly ok. There are few fairly bad ones (Magician and Moon being the biggest examples), and the Protag has very little impact on a lot of them - if not outright negative impact (like Hanged and Chariot, with the Protag acting like an enabler for bad behavior). There are great ones as well, though, like Sun (fantastic - my favorite in the game), Lovers and Aeon.

The Linked Episodes are awesome though, and I enjoy the Dorm activities quite a lot. Even the Koromaru walks end up having pretty nice dialogues.

While the base game is quite good, the DLC is fantastic. The biggest emotional pay-outs of the game happen in the DLC, some VERY IMPORTANT character arc conclusions also happen in the DLC, to the point that I actually think it's kinda b…
Probably one of my favorite stories in a game ngl. Tartarus is a little repetitive but the payoff for getting through it was more than worth it for me.

citations.review_text: Base game is amazing, with only a few baffling situations like the power balance with a gun involved. That being said, easy 8/10 game, but it is massively brought down by the absolutely disappointing overpriced dlc. Thankfully Steam allows us to separate the base game from the dlc, so I don't have to put it on this one, but word to the wise: do not get the dlc unless you want to 100% the achievements, just youtube the 30ish minutes of cutscenes and save yourself $35.

After months of playing traditional JRPGs, I finally decided to jump into the Persona franchise for the very first time.
Before this, I had never touched a single Persona game in any shape or form.

To be honest, I was initially skeptical about the "unique" visuals and UI.
However, I eventually realized that this game is absolutely worth playing.

The music is incredibly cool—I'm not gonna lie—though unfortunately, the best tracks only play in specific areas.

The graphics aren't exactly top-tier, but they are decent enough for a remake.

In my personal opinion, grinding in this game doesn't feel too tedious.
Even though Tartarus is highly repetitive, your efforts feel rewarding based on what you get out of it.

The character development is also phenomenal.
Every single party member and friend you make literally has their own distinct story, covering their past and their personal growth as they face the conflicts that surface.
This is exactly what allows you to understand them on a much deeper level.

The only highly frustrating part is that I had to purchase the "epilogue" as a separate DLC, even though I already bought the Digital Premium Edition.

And congratulations to all the completionists out there: certain achievements required for the Platinum trophy can only be unlocked if you buy that DLC.
Pretty sickening, isn't it?
